aufgaben.ausgang: Decide whether the statements are true or false. If false, write the correct answer.

teile.text: 1.1 The term synchronic describes a specific point in time, while diachronic describes language change through time.
1.2 Function denotes a speaker’s ability to only be able to convey basic messages, while form denotes a mastery over the language.
teile.tipp1: Is the pair about the speaker’s skill?
teile.loesung: b) False. Correct answer: Form refers to the structure of language (sounds, word forms, sentence patterns), function refers to what a form is used for in communication, i.e. its purpose (e.g. “Can you open the window?” = question form, request function).

teile.text: 1.3 Applied linguistics refers to studies that still have real-life applications, ‘not applied’ refers to studies in the past that are not in use anymore.
teile.tipp1: Is the difference about time or about the goal?
teile.tipp2: Theoretical linguistics studies language for its own sake.
teile.loesung: b) False. Correct answer: Applied linguistics uses linguistic findings to solve practical, real-life problems (e.g. language teaching, translation, speech therapy). ‘Not applied’ (theoretical) linguistics studies language for its own sake to describe and explain how it works.

aufgaben.titel: Schools of thought – fill in the gaps
aufgaben.ausgang: Complete the texts from the worksheet and label the model of the sign.

teile.text: 2.1 Structuralism: This is a school of thought that stems from the work of ____ (~1900). In structuralism, linguists are primarily concerned with the abstract language system shared by all members of a speech community, called ____, and less so about ____, which is about the concrete usage of language by the individual.
2.1 (figure) Label the sign /frɒg/: signifié (signified) = ____ ; ____ = the sound image, i.e. that which signifies.
teile.tipp1: The upper half shows the frog idea.
teile.loesung: signifié = the concept / mental idea, i.e. that which is signified · signifiant (signifier) = the sound image

teile.text: 2.2 Formalism: This school of thought is widely associated with ____ work in the 1950s and 1960s. He views every human as being born with a ____, i.e. humans are viewed as genetically predisposed to learn language. This is based on the theory of ____ which consists of syntactic structures and constraints that are thought to be universal in human languages and, thus, innate.
2.3 Formalism (Roman Jakobson 1920s): Name three linguistic disciplines that formalism heavily influenced.

aufgaben.ausgang: A fellow student missed the session. Explain the key concepts to her in your own words – in English, with one example each.

teile.text: Explain form vs. function using a sentence of your choice.
teile.tipp1: Choose a question that is not really a question.
teile.loesung:
• Form = structure: “Can you pass the salt?” is an interrogative sentence (yes/no question).
  • Function = purpose: it is used as a polite request.
  • One form can have several functions, one function several forms.

teile.text: Explain Saussure’s linguistic sign using the word “tree”.
teile.tipp1: Two sides of one sheet of paper.
teile.loesung:
• signifié: the concept/idea of a tree
  • signifiant: the sound image /triː/
  • the link is arbitrary (German: Baum)

• Saussure: langue = shared abstract system (social), parole = concrete individual use.
  • Chomsky: competence = unconscious grammar knowledge (mental, individual), performance = actual use.
  • Both focus on the system (langue / competence).
